comparison_author_model: Stage 1A used GPT-5.6 Luna; model versions differ.

determinism.scene_script: same inputs and Blender version rebuild the same geometry
determinism.obj_byte_hashes: house, tower and ship matched on two runs; statue and dragon OBJ face order varied, while named objects, vertex data and canonical triangle geometry matched
determinism.voxelplan_byte_hashes: all ten surface/solid VoxelPlans matched on two adapter runs

cases.brief: Create a compact two-storey timber house with a rectangular footprint, visible entrance, windows, and a pitched roof. Keep the roof, walls, and openings easy to distinguish from outside.

repair_rounds.reason: MinePilot preview showed the exported Y axis reversed, placing the roof at the base.
repair_rounds.result: Changed OBJ forward/up mapping; vertex bounds are now Y=0..64 and both Blender/voxel previews are upright.

repair_rounds.reason: MinePilot front view showed a valley roof rather than a pitched ridge.
repair_rounds.result: Reversed the two roof slab rotations; the preview now shows a peaked roof attached to the upper walls.

repair_rounds.reason: Initial EEVEE render was too dark and viewed the back facade.
repair_rounds.result: Used a material-colored Workbench studio pass and a front-facing camera; source evidence is readable, voxel geometry is unchanged.

cases.minecraft_usefulness: BORDERLINE: pitched roof and two storeys read, but the single stone palette obscures the shallow door/window inserts and the solid plan is block-heavy.
cases.visual_reason: Final MinePilot front view preserves a pitched roof and house massing. The uniform stone palette and filled wall volumes make the facade openings faint; solid occupancy is 43% higher than Stage 1A.

cases.brief: Create a single medieval stone watchtower with a broad base, tall shaft, an upper lookout, battlements, and a narrow entrance. Keep the vertical tower silhouette clear.

repair_rounds.reason: MinePilot preview showed the exported Y axis reversed.
repair_rounds.result: Changed OBJ forward/up mapping; Blender render and VoxelPlan now keep the lookout and battlements above the base.

repair_rounds.reason: The initial EEVEE render was under-lit.
repair_rounds.result: Switched to a material-colored Workbench studio pass; MinePilot geometry and block counts were unchanged.

cases.minecraft_usefulness: PASS: the broad base, vertical shaft, lookout and merlons form a useful simple watchtower; door and slit details fade in the uniform stone output.
cases.visual_reason: MinePilot views preserve the upright cylindrical tower and battlements. Dimensions and solid occupancy are almost identical to Stage 1A; this family does not show a meaningful DCC advantage.

cases.brief: Create a small wooden sailing ship with a tapered hull, deck, one mast, and two sails. Make the hull and mast readable from the side and three-quarter views.

repair_rounds.reason: The first ship OBJ had an out-of-range face index from the hand-built two-vertex hull cross-section.
repair_rounds.result: Rebuilt each station as a three-vertex V keel and closed the longitudinal faces; OBJ export and the #116 adapter then succeeded.

repair_rounds.reason: MinePilot preview showed the exported Y axis reversed.
repair_rounds.result: Changed OBJ forward/up mapping; mast and hull now retain the same upright axis and the boat is not inverted.

repair_rounds.reason: The initial EEVEE source render was too dark for review.
repair_rounds.result: Used the Workbench material/studio render pass; geometry and voxel output were unchanged.

voxelizer_failures: Initial pre-repair OBJ: adapter rejected a face index on line 37 (out of range); fixed in Blender scene geometry, no adapter changes.
cases.minecraft_usefulness: BORDERLINE: mast and sails survive, but the hull is a shallow rectangular mass and open sail sheets do not create filled volume in solid mode.
major_lost_details: Two distinct sail planes in solid fill
cases.visual_reason: The MinePilot front/three-quarter view reads as a mast-and-sail boat, but the low hull profile remains shallow. Open sail meshes contribute surface coverage only, so geometric/source improvements to sails partly disappear in solid occupancy.

cases.brief: Create a monumental standing humanoid statue on a simple plinth, with a distinct head, torso, two arms, and two legs. Keep the pose and body parts readable at a distance.

repair_rounds.reason: MinePilot preview showed the OBJ Y axis reversed, putting the head at the base.
repair_rounds.result: Changed exporter axis mapping and verified Y=0..64; the statue is upright in both Blender and MinePilot.

repair_rounds.reason: The initial EEVEE source render was nearly black.
repair_rounds.result: Changed source evidence to a material-colored Workbench studio render; VoxelPlan occupancy was unchanged.

cases.minecraft_usefulness: PASS: a readable standing humanoid monument on a plinth; arms project clearly from the torso in the front preview, while face and clothing detail are absent.
cases.visual_reason: The front MinePilot preview reads as a standing figure with a separated head, lateral arms, legs and a stepped base. Occupancy is very close to Stage 1A while the arms read more clearly at a distance.

cases.brief: Create a perched fantasy dragon facing sideways, with a distinct head and neck, body, four legs, long tail, and two large wings. Favor a strong outer silhouette over tiny scales or spikes.

repair_rounds.reason: MinePilot preview showed the OBJ Y axis reversed, placing raised wings and the head below the body.
repair_rounds.result: Changed exporter axis mapping; body, head, tail and wings now share upright Y=0..64 bounds.

repair_rounds.reason: The first source render was too dark to judge the broad wing planes.
repair_rounds.result: Used a material-colored Workbench studio render. This improved source inspection; voxel geometry was unchanged.

cases.minecraft_usefulness: BORDERLINE: a recognizable side-profile dragon with a prominent wing, head, body, tail and legs; paired wings/limbs merge into one broad solid form and the depth consumes 2.5× Stage 1A solid blocks.
cases.visual_reason: The MinePilot front view preserves a strong organic dragon silhouette and broad wings, a DCC strength over the thin Stage 1A profile. In isometric/solid view the far wing and limbs merge with the body, and the 60-block depth raises occupancy substantially.

environment_friction: No Blender CLI was on PATH; Blender 5.2.2 LTS was downloaded and run from an isolated application path.
Blender CLI and the PyPI bpy 5.2.2 module both failed inside the sandbox during native Metal/architecture initialization; Blender headless CLI succeeded outside the sandbox, without GUI interaction.

The initial source script used incompatible Blender 5.2 engine, OBJ axis and cylinder-operator enum/property names. One axis guess inverted all models; Y bounds inspection identified forward_axis=Y, up_axis=Z as the correct mapping for these Y-up scenes.

No MinePilot content was published. A temporary local-only review page called the existing MinePilot createVoxelPreview production renderer; its temporary route/data were removed after screenshot capture.
semantic_scene_value: Named Blender objects and collections carry useful bounded labels (walls/roof/openings, hull/deck/sails, body/wings/legs). The OBJ exporter preserves object group names, but the #116 adapter flattens the OBJ into one VoxelPlan and drops those labels. These are potential future compile hints; they do not justify mesh-to-ComponentPlan reverse engineering.
strongest_blender_advantage: The dragon (and, to a lesser degree, statue) could be assembled and revised as a named 3D scene with separate organic masses and wing membranes. The dragon's broad three-dimensional wing silhouette remains recognizable in MinePilot where Stage 1A is a thinner profile.
strongest_blender_disadvantage: Scene/export state and axis conventions added a real debugging tax: the first apparently valid OBJ coordinates inverted all five previews, Blender API changes broke first runs, and the ship's custom mesh initially emitted an invalid face. Organic breadth also increased dragon solid blocks from 17,485 to 44,203.
recommendation: Keep Blender as an optional upstream mesh producer for freeform organic silhouettes, with scripted/headless authoring and strict OBJ bounds checks. Do not replace ComponentPlan for houses/towers; current procedural route is shorter and produces equivalent or more efficient structures. Preserve named scene groups as optional bounded hints only if a later adapter needs them.
issue_114_recommendation: Proceed only with a narrow implementation follow-up for DCC-authored freeform input. The benchmark supports a useful Blender route for dragon/statue, but does not justify expanding the core DSL or productionizing generic scene semantics yet.
